title: VS Code Exercises
description: Practise the ideas from this VS Code course. Each answer has an explanation to help you learn.

exercises.question: What is VS Code primarily?
exercises.explanation: Visual Studio Code is a code editor. It helps you read and change files, but it is not the same thing as a browser or every language's runtime. Each tool has a different job. This course focuses on the editor and safe local practice files.

exercises.question: Why open a folder?
options: To work with related project files
exercises.explanation: Opening a folder gives the editor a workspace for related files. Use a new folder made only for learning. The Explorer can show the page and stylesheet together. A folder name helps you recognise the project.

exercises.question: What does the Command Palette search?
exercises.explanation: The Command Palette searches editor actions by name. It is useful when you do not remember a menu location. The palette helps find actions. A command's availability can depend on the current file and installed extensions.

exercises.question: Which name is an HTML file?
exercises.explanation: A file extension helps the editor choose language support. Saving changes writes them to disk; an unsaved tab can differ from the saved file. The extension communicates the file type. The editor's language mode can also be selected manually.

exercises.question: What does whole-word search avoid here?
exercises.explanation: Find locates matching text in the current file. Check match-case and whole-word settings when results seem surprising. Search settings change what counts as a match.

exercises.question: Does a workspace search always include every file on disk?
exercises.explanation: Workspace search finds text in several files. Review the included and excluded paths before trusting the result. The results show file names and matching lines. They help you find all visible uses of a phrase.

exercises.question: What should happen before Replace All?
exercises.explanation: Replace changes text. Review each match or the preview before applying many changes at once. A small preview helps avoid changing unrelated sentences or variable names.

exercises.question: What does formatting mainly change?
exercises.explanation: A formatter adjusts layout such as indentation. It should preserve the intended program behaviour. The formatter used depends on the language and setup. The spaces improve readability; the object still stores the same value.

exercises.question: Where do these project settings commonly live?
exercises.explanation: Workspace settings apply to the project. A .vscode/settings.json file can record a few agreed editor choices. Word wrapping makes long lines easier to see. Format on save uses an available configured formatter.

exercises.question: Is the integrated terminal only a pretend shell?
exercises.explanation: The integrated terminal is a real shell inside the editor window. Its commands can change files just like any other terminal. The terminal is convenient but still powerful. Know which project folder it is using.

exercises.question: What should guide workspace trust?
options: Whether you understand and trust the project
exercises.explanation: Extensions add editor features. Workspace Trust helps decide whether code in a folder may activate potentially risky features. The decision is about the project source, not whether its icon looks familiar. Install only extensions you need from a trusted publisher.

exercises.question: What does a breakpoint do?
exercises.explanation: A debugger can pause a supported program and let you inspect values. A breakpoint marks a place to pause. Setup depends on the language runtime. The debugger makes the program's state visible one step at a time. It does not decide what the correct result should be.
